# Rewiring the enterprise: AI-native growth

> A leadership brief on where evidence, specialist judgment, and delivery now create advantage.
> 28 July 2026

## Executive perspective

The next cycle of advantage will belong to organizations that combine proprietary evidence, specialist judgment, and rapid execution. Scale still matters, but it no longer compensates for slow decisions or generic delivery.

> [!METRIC]
> **2.4×**
> Higher renewal intent when specialist expertise is embedded with client teams.

> [!INSIGHT]
> The scarce asset is no longer capacity. It is judgment applied early enough to change the decision.

### What leaders should know

Three signals matter most:

1. Buyers are unbundling broad mandates into smaller, outcome-specific assignments.
2. Embedded expertise is outperforming episodic advice.
3. Reusable evidence is compressing the path from uncertainty to action.

## Market structure

Value is migrating from broad delivery capacity toward specialized capability. The strongest positions combine a focused point of view with repeatable evidence and delivery close to the decision.

| Signal | What changed | Leadership implication |
|---|---|---|
| Buyer pull | Mandates are narrower and more consequential | Compete on the quality of the decision |
| Talent model | Senior specialists stay close to delivery | Put expertise inside the operating rhythm |
| Asset leverage | Reusable evidence shortens analysis cycles | Invest in proprietary research systems |

> [!TAKEAWAY]
> Organize the offer around the moments where evidence can still change the path.

## Evidence landscape

Evidence is most valuable when it arrives in time to influence the choice. A large archive does not create an advantage by itself; the differentiator is the ability to retrieve, test, and apply the right evidence quickly.

### Confidence and limits

The directional pattern is strong, but adoption will vary by regulation, data access, organizational design, and the cost of integrating new systems into established workflows.

## Strategic options

Leaders have three practical choices. They can improve the existing model, build a specialist capability alongside it, or redesign the operating system around AI-native research and decision support.

### Option A — strengthen the core

Upgrade research operations, codify reusable methods, and give teams a shared evidence standard.

### Option B — build a specialist engine

Create small expert teams that own narrow problems, proprietary datasets, and repeatable decision tools.

### Option C — redesign the system

Integrate research, synthesis, judgment, and production into one operating loop with clear human accountability.

## Recommendations

Start with decisions that are frequent, expensive, and evidence-sensitive. Establish a baseline, test the new model against a real operating choice, and expand only when the evidence shows a meaningful improvement.

1. Select one high-value decision.
2. Build the smallest reusable evidence asset that can improve it.
3. Keep senior judgment close to the work.
4. Measure decision speed, confidence, and downstream results.
